facts.fact: Cybernetica says that in 2014 it and the e-Governance Academy introduced an interoperability platform, known locally as Nam-X, connecting databases of different entities, and that Namibia has implemented it for secure data exchange between organisations.

Cybernetica says an ESTDEV-funded project begun in 2024 continues scaling the Nam-X platform, developing two digital services for it, and was expected to end in March 2025; no count of connected bodies is given.

systems.owner: Office of the Prime Minister, Department of Public Service e-Government Management

slug: 2020-01-24 Namibia Case Study Highlights Importance of Data Policy Alignment for SDG 16.9

facts.fact: The IISD report on a Global Partnership for Sustainable Development Data compendium says the e-birth and e-death notification platforms are linked to the National Population Registration System through the National Data Exchange Service Bus interoperability layer, which also lets the register link to other government and private-sector registers; no date for the link is given and the count of connected systems is not stated.

note: as_of is the published date, the document giving no event date.

slug: 2016-12-01 Governmental Interoperability in Namibia - E-riigi Akadeemia

facts.fact: The e-Governance Academy says its project, run October 2014 to December 2016, delivered an X-Road-based interoperability framework using Cybernetica's UXP technology to connect government databases, in three stages ending in full-scale implementation; it does not say the platform was in service.

The World Bank blog says Namibia adopted the Estonian open-source X-Road software after 2011, so the National Population Register now links functional public and private sector registries, and it was used during COVID-19 to validate identity data for emergency income support.

note: Adoption year given only as after 2011 and present tense; published date used as as_of.

systems.owner: Office of the Prime Minister, DPSITM

note: The EOI says Namibia adopted X-Road and the EEC envisages exchanging data through the government platform, but gives no statement of the platform's status, reach or use.

slug: 2025-09-03 Season 3 - Namibia's Digital Identity Journey - From Vision to Reality (UNDP)

facts.fact: The government is deploying NamX, a data-exchange platform for secure inter-ministry sharing, per UNDP Namibia.

note: as_of is the document's published date, 2025-09-03; it gives no event date.
Nam-X is named a platform with no description of what it does or whether it carries data between public bodies; the project adds two digital services to it.
Two agencies signed an MoU and name integrating their systems a long-term goal; no data exchange platform is stated.
The document mentions no government data exchange platform; it says no law or MoU on migration data exchange exists.
The claim is already held in evidence.csv.

systems.owner: Ministry of Information and Communication Technology

note: In service already held as NAM-001.

facts.fact: The Namibia Statistics Agency says a National Data Exchange Platform is being developed with Estonia, with infrastructure and connection established and NamRA as first testing point, then the Office of the Prime Minister for CRVS data; partners include the Bank of Namibia and Ministry of Home Affairs.
